results.question: When do I send my first unemployment status report to Kela?
results.answer: In your first application, you report your unemployment dates starting from your first day of unemployment [S1]. To get your first benefit payment, you must submit an unemployment status report covering a 2-week period after filing your first application [S1][S6]. You can only report days that have already passed [S1][S3].

results.question: I'm 22 and have no vocational qualification. Do I have to apply for studies to get the benefit?
results.answer: Yes, if you are under 25 and do not have a vocational qualification or higher education degree, you must apply for admission to at least two education programmes that begin in the autumn term [S2][S5][S8]. You must also participate in any entrance exam you are invited to [S2][S8]. You should contact employment services to agree on these education applications in more detail [S2][S8].

results.question: I'm 61 and long-term unemployed. For how long can a pay subsidy be granted?
results.answer: A pay subsidy may be granted for hiring a long-term unemployed person aged 60 or over for a maximum of 24 months at a time [S1]. The subsidy is granted for the duration of the employment relationship at most [S1]. The employment authority decides the duration of each support period separately based on your service need [S1][S2].

results.question: Can I get my travel costs paid when I go to an aptitude test for labour market training?
results.answer: Yes, as an unemployed jobseeker, you can apply for reimbursement of travel and accommodation expenses from the employment authority when you travel for an aptitude test or admission event for labour market training [S1][S4]. Reimbursement requires that the employment authority considers it appropriate for the availability of labour and your employment [S8].

results.question: Kela paid me labour market subsidy before May 2026. Will they check my income now?
results.answer:
If Kela paid you labour market subsidy without a means test before you transferred to the general social security benefit on 1 May 2026, Kela will check your income by 30 September 2026 to see how much of it affects the means test [S2]. 
Kela will contact you if necessary before applying the means test, and you will receive a separate decision notice if your benefit is reduced [S2]. 
This means test only affects future payments and does not reduce your benefit retroactively [S2].

Note: The labour market subsidy was abolished when Kela began paying the general social security benefit on 1 May 2026. [S9]

results.question: what is yleistuki
results.answer:
The general social security benefit (*yleistuki*) is a new financial assistance introduced for unemployed jobseekers [S2]. 

You can receive it if you are 18–64 years old, live permanently in Finland, are registered as an unemployed jobseeker with employment services, and cannot get or have run out of earnings-related unemployment allowance [S5]. It replaces the labour market subsidy and basic unemployment allowance [S2]. 

You must apply for it from Kela [S2]. It is paid 5 days a week based on an unemployment status report [S5], and you must be available for work on the labour market to receive it [S6]. Earned income, parents' income if you live with them, and certain other benefits reduce the amount, while housing allowance and child benefits do not [S1][S7].
